centralQuestion: Do neoplastic cells in Vehicle and PLX-treated tumours have different nuclear morphologies?
centralAnswer: In this eight-mouse pilot, neoplastic-cell morphology differs across tissue environments, but the data do not establish one consistent PLX-associated morphology change across matched environments.
audience: Biologists, pathologists and clinically oriented collaborators; no computational-science background assumed.
studyDesignNote: Eight mice contribute one whole-slide image each (four Vehicle and four PLX4720 overall; two per arm within each cohort). Results are exploratory; tiles and nuclei are subsamples, not independent treatment replicates. Combined inference is cohort-blocked with equal cohort weight; naive pooled 4-vs-4 inference is not performed.

conceptualModel.label: Why the main question must be separated
conceptualModel.equation: Observed whole-tumour morphology difference = tissue-environment mixture difference + within-matched-environment cell difference + mouse/slide/stain/segmentation variation

terms.explanation: A tumour can look different because it contains different proportions of pale, mixed, cohesive or elongated-looking H&E environments.

terms.plain_label: Cells differ within the same environment
terms.explanation: A treatment-associated cell-shape change is most credible if it appears when like tissue environments are compared with like.
With one slide per mouse, animal biology cannot be separated fully from section, stain, scan and segmentation variation.

eccentricity.direction: Higher values indicate a more elongated outline.

axis_ratio.direction: Higher values indicate a more elongated outline.
axis_ratio.caveat: A deterministic re-expression of eccentricity, not independent confirmation.

area.direction: Higher values indicate a larger segmented nuclear profile.

equivalent_diameter.direction: Higher values indicate a larger segmented nuclear profile.
equivalent_diameter.caveat: Derived directly from area, not independent confirmation.

perimeter.direction: Higher values indicate a longer segmented nuclear boundary.

compactness.direction: Higher values indicate a more compact, circle-like outline.

solidity.direction: Lower values indicate a more indented or irregular outline.

evidenceJourney.title: First, do the tumours look different when tissue context is ignored?
evidenceJourney.motivation: A whole-tumour comparison is the intuitive starting point, but it mixes every tissue environment in a slide.
evidenceJourney.question: Across the eight mice, are overall neoplastic nuclear measurements shifted between Vehicle and PLX4720?
evidenceJourney.method: For each mouse, apply the post-hoc C0/C1/C2/C6 whole-tumour response population. Within every morphology-evaluable tile containing at least one eligible high-confidence, non-edge neoplastic nucleus, calculate the within-tile median and then average those tile medians equally. Compare the eight mouse-level values with treatment labels permuted within each cohort (36 legal 2+2×2+2 allocations) and weight the two cohort effects equally; do not perform a naive pooled 4-vs-4 test.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Show one dot per mouse in small metric panels, with Vehicle and PLX4720 separated. Display the PLX-minus-Vehicle difference and exact eight-mouse permutation result as context, not as a discovery threshold.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: Any restricted cellular-tissue difference is a candidate signal only: it may reflect altered C3/C4/C5/C2/C6 mixture, a within-context cell change, or mouse/slide variation.

result.summary: Within the post-hoc exploratory C0/C1/C2/C6 composition-sensitive whole-tumour response population, tile-balanced nuclear elongation differed by -0.0013 (PLX4720 minus Vehicle); the exact cohort-blocked permutation p-value was 0.889 across 36 legal within-cohort allocations.
result.interpretation: This observed-mixture contrast combines context mixture and within-context morphology. It weights only C0/C1/C2/C6 tiles with an evaluable high-confidence neoplastic morphology value, so it is exploratory rather than a treatment-effect estimate.

pooledInference.reason: No naive 4-vs-4 pooled inference is performed. Treatment labels are permuted within each 2-vs-2 cohort and cohort-specific effects receive equal weight.

evidenceJourney.title: What tissue environments are present in these sections?
evidenceJourney.motivation: Neoplastic nuclear shape depends on the surrounding architecture, so biologically meaningful comparison requires a map of recurring H&E environments.
evidenceJourney.question: What does each image-derived cluster appear to represent, where does it occur, and how confidently can it be named?
evidenceJourney.method: Group UNI-v2 tile embeddings without using treatment labels or nuclear outcomes, then inspect representative tiles, slide locations, cell composition and morphology. Keep pathology names provisional until expert review.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Show phenotype cards with full-resolution examples, slide locations, tile and nucleus coverage, morphology fingerprints and a three-level identity statement: technical description, candidate biological interpretation, pathologist confirmation status.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: The clusters are recurring H&E image phenotypes, not proven anatomical compartments. Blank/background is not a biological morphology group, and all biological labels remain provisional.
evidenceJourney.advanced_detail: Technical appendix: how the seven image phenotypes were selected

result.summary: The frozen map contains 7 tissue-image phenotypes (C0/C1/C2/C3/C4/C5/C6). The whole-tumour response population contains C0/C1/C2/C6; matched shared-context inference uses C0/C1/C2/C6.
result.interpretation: Every cluster has a pathology-informed candidate interpretation, but none is pathologist-confirmed. Numeric C# labels remain run-local.

evidenceJourney.title: Do Vehicle and PLX4720 tumours contain different mixtures of tissue environments?
evidenceJourney.motivation: A change in tumour architecture can shift whole-slide nuclear summaries even when cells do not change within matched environments.
evidenceJourney.question: Does the proportion of tiles assigned to each tissue environment differ between treatment arms?
evidenceJourney.method: Within each mouse, count all reviewed biological C0, C1, C2 and C6 tiles and renormalise their fractions so C0+C1+C2+C6 equals 100%. Compare arms with the cohort-blocked equal-cohort 2×2×2 design; if either cohort is incomplete the inferential result is N/A. tiles are not treatment replicates.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Use 100% stacked bars for the four individual mice and a separate dot plot of C3/C4/C5/C2/C6 PLX-minus-Vehicle percentage-point differences. Label the denominator as the share of C3/C4/C5/C2/C6 tiles; do not mix C3/C4/C5 into treatment-facing plots.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: Report candidate architecture shifts by cluster, but do not describe them as independent treatment effects or as proof of drug response.

result.summary: Within all reviewed biological C0+C1+C2+C6 tiles, the largest arm difference was C1: -16.78 percentage points (PLX4720 minus Vehicle).
result.interpretation: These are all-tile architecture proportions, not the morphology-evaluable weights used in Question 1. They sum to 100% within mouse and are exploratory under the cohort-blocked equal-cohort design.

evidenceJourney.title: Do neoplastic nuclei naturally differ between tissue environments?
evidenceJourney.motivation: Stratification is useful only if image environments correspond to interpretable differences in the nuclei they contain.
evidenceJourney.question: Across all slides, which nuclear measurements distinguish the biological tile clusters, and do those differences recur across mice?
evidenceJourney.method: For C0/C1/C2/C6, assign each eligible detected nucleus to its containing tile, summarise nuclei within tiles and tiles within mice, and compare mouse-balanced profiles. Keep injury-like residual nuclei descriptive and test the shared-context tile classifier by leaving one entire mouse/WSI out; C0, C1 and C2 is flagged as coverage-limited.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Use a cluster-by-metric effect heatmap for the overview, mouse-balanced distributions for a selected metric, eight mouse dots for recurrence, and held-out-mouse confusion matrices for classification. Never connect unordered clusters with lines.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: Morphology that distinguishes embedding clusters supports biological concordance, not independent validation: both tile embeddings and nuclear features come from the same H&E sections.

result.summary: Across C0/C1/C2/C6, the equal-mouse elongation profile was highest in C0 (0.7819) and lowest in C2 (0.7196). The held-out-mouse context classifier was N/A because the complete run-local class set was not represented in every fold.
result.interpretation: C0/C1/C2/C6 residual-nucleus morphology is descriptively associated with image context, and the classifier is not independent pathology validation because both measurements come from the same H&E sections.

evidenceJourney.title: Within the same tissue environment, does PLX4720 alter neoplastic nuclear morphology?
evidenceJourney.motivation: Matching tissue context separates a possible cell-level change from a change in the amount of each environment.
evidenceJourney.question: For each supported cluster and morphology metric, is the PLX-minus-Vehicle direction consistent across mice?
evidenceJourney.method: Within the shared contexts C0, C1, C2 and C6, calculate one equal-tile morphology summary per mouse. Compare the eight mouse-level values with treatment labels permuted within each cohort (36 legal 2+2×2+2 allocations) and weight the two cohort effects equally; do not perform a naive pooled 4-vs-4 test. Fully supported contexts are C0/C1/C2/C6. C0, C1 and C2 remains descriptive with treatment p-values shown as N/A.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Use a cluster-by-metric treatment-effect heatmap. Selecting a cell must reveal the four raw mouse dots, sample coverage and robustness status; unsupported cells display N/A rather than zero.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: A credible shared treatment phenotype would require comparable directions across supported contexts and mice. Heterogeneous directions argue against a cluster-invariant effect in this pilot.

evidenceJourney.title: Does the treatment contrast remain after equalising tissue-environment mixture?
evidenceJourney.motivation: Standardisation asks what the overall comparison would look like if every mouse contributed the same supported cluster mixture.
evidenceJourney.question: How does the overall morphology contrast change under equal-cluster and pooled-reference weighting?
evidenceJourney.method: Compare each mouse's observed composition-sensitive C0/C1/C2/C6 mixture with the explicitly non-estimable equal-C0/C1/C2/C6 view, then show equal C0/C1/C2/C6 as the common-support sensitivity. Decompose the observed contrast descriptively without causal attribution. Use cohort-blocked equal-cohort effects for Combined.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Use aligned observed-mixture, equal-C0/C1/C2/C6 and equal-C0/C1/C2/C6 mouse-dot panels on one scale, plus a clearly non-causal descriptive decomposition.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: If standardised estimates remain mouse-sensitive or disagree across contexts, the data do not support a composition-independent treatment effect.

result.summary: Observed composition-sensitive C0/C1/C2/C6 elongation differed by -0.0013. Equal C0/C1/C2/C6 weighting was N/A; the shared-context equal-C0/C1/C2/C6 sensitivity was N/A.
result.interpretation: The C0/C1/C2/C6 standardisation is descriptive. Reweighting therefore does not establish a composition-independent PLX4720 morphology effect.

evidenceJourney.title: What do these eight mice allow us to conclude?
evidenceJourney.motivation: The final claim must reflect biological evidence, experimental replication and technical uncertainty together.
evidenceJourney.question: Which observations are supported, which are hypotheses, and what evidence is still needed?
evidenceJourney.method: Use the Stage 24 claim matrix to triangulate restricted composition, cross-context morphology, matched-context effects, standardisation and support limitations while preserving mouse as the experimental unit.
evidenceJourney.result_prompt: Show a claim-evidence matrix with Supported observation, Candidate hypothesis, Not established and Next validation columns. Keep technical sensitivity tables collapsible.
evidenceJourney.interpretation: Current evidence supports heterogeneous tissue contexts and context-associated nuclear morphology. It does not establish a causal, cluster-invariant PLX-induced nuclear phenotype.

result.summary: Stage 24 supports internal cross-mouse concordance between cellular image contexts and nuclear morphology, identifies only exploratory context-mixture differences, and does not establish one shared within-context PLX4720 effect.
result.interpretation: Replication with more mice and arm-blinded pathologist review of the phenotype identities are required before causal, mechanistic, or clinical claims.
